audit_findings.title: Equity-method stakes may be counted twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $229 million of 2025 equity-method earnings, $201 million of 2025 distributions, and a $1,341 million stake bridge addition; exact overlap unquantified. If the full $229 million remained in anchor OE, purging it would reduce base value by approximately $3.79 per share and the buy-below threshold by approximately $2.65 per share.
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method earnings or distributions enter OE while the ownership interests are separately added through stakes_net in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Under this method of accounting, the Company’s share of the net earnings or losses of the investee is presented within Operating profit on the Consolidated Statement of Operations since the activities of the investee are closely aligned with the operations of the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that investee earnings are included in operating profit and that distributions were received, while the valuation demonstrably adds $1,341 million for stakes. Double counting is not yet demonstrated because the OE workpaper showing any purge was not supplied. Nevertheless, full overlap would reduce the base valuation by about 11%, enough to materially change the estimated value and purchase threshold.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each component of the $1,341 million stakes_net to the $229 million earnings and $201 million distributions, then rerun OE after purging the amounts attributable to separately valued stakes.

audit_findings.title: Parent-common OE mixes ownership bases
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed reference points are $103 million of 2025 NCI earnings, $67 million for the first half of 2026, and $325 million of NCI equity at June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable earnings are combined with consolidated depreciation, capital expenditures, working-capital flows, cash and other assets that may partly belong to non-controlling owners.
audit_findings.evidence: A non-controlling interest in a subsidiary is considered an ownership interest in a majority-owned subsidiary that is not attributable to the parent.
audit_findings.explanation: The ownership-basis mismatch is demonstrated, but its net valuation effect is not. Consolidated add-backs and cash can overstate the parent claim, while consolidated capital expenditures can understate it. The filed NCI figures show a real claim, but they do not identify the NCI share of each OE or bridge component, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a parent-claim schedule allocating every OE adjustment, capital expenditure, working-capital amount and bridge asset to Carrier common owners; alternatively estimate and deduct the fair value of the complete NCI claim, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Riello sale is missing from the perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $430 million gross proceeds, a $46 million impairment, and $422 million of net held-for-sale assets at December 31, 2025; the gross proceeds equal about $0.51 per diluted share and 1.5% of base equity value. Riello OE is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-sale OE should exclude Riello, while net sale proceeds should enter the equity bridge without also retaining Riello earnings or assets.
audit_findings.evidence: This transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2026 and is subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter error is demonstrated: the sale closed July 1, 2026, before the September 5 valuation, while the perimeter is null and the bridge uses June 30 cash that precedes receipt of proceeds. The upward component is limited by the filed $430 million gross proceeds to about $0.51 per share, versus the $20.49 gap between the $59.71 price and $39.22 bull value. Removing Riello earnings would move value downward, so this item cannot reverse the investment conclusion on the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 1 closing statement and Riello's 2025 and 2026 OE contribution, replace Riello with actual net proceeds in a documented pro-forma perimeter, and confirm that proceeds were not otherwise included.

audit_findings.title: Unpaid AFFF settlement is a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $615 million recorded liability, comprising $565 million recorded in 2024 plus $50 million recorded at deconsolidation; the agreements also commit estimated $115 million of KFI sale proceeds and the first $125 million of specified insurance proceeds. The June 30, 2026 unpaid net obligation and residual claims are unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Unpaid settlement cash and residual legal claims reduce the equity bridge or future OE, while insurance recoveries not otherwise recognized would increase the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As part of the Proposed Settlement Agreements, the Company will pay $ 615 million in cash over five years, 100 % of the net sale proceeds from its sale of KFI’s assets to Pacific Avenue Capital Partners, which are estimated to be $ 115 million, and contribute the right to recover proceeds under certain of its insurance policies.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual claim is demonstrated, but the amount still unpaid at the valuation date is not supplied. Even the full $615 million corporate-cash amount is about $0.72 per share, or 2.1% of base equity value, which alone is not material. A NOT_MATERIAL conclusion is unavailable because insurance recoveries, court approvals and non-settling or residual claims remain unresolved and the filing states that additional exposure cannot be estimated and could be material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30 liability roll-forward, payments made through September 5, court-approval status, KFI proceeds and actual or probable insurance recoveries; deduct the net unpaid obligation and separately sensitivity-test unquantified residual claims.

audit_findings.title: Discrete 2025 tax benefits may inflate the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $129 million total filed benefits: $64 million German, $49 million Japanese reorganization and $16 million purchased tax credits. This equals 7.0% of anchor OE; full removal would reduce bear/base/bull values by approximately $1.81/$2.13/$2.52 per share and reduce the base buy-below threshold by approximately $1.49 per share.
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-recurring tax benefits raise the latest-year OE anchor and are consequently capitalized through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease was primarily driven by a net tax benefit of $64 million from changes to the German effective rate and a statutory reduction to the German corporate tax rate enacted during the year, a tax benefit of $49 million from the re-organization of a Japanese subsidiary and a $16 million tax benefit generated by the purchase of investment tax credits from a third-party.
audit_findings.explanation: The tax benefits are demonstrated, but their inclusion in OE and the one-time portion of the German benefit are unresolved because the tax-normalization workpaper is absent. Their quantified scale is material: full inclusion would overstate base value by about 6.3% and meaningfully change the purchase threshold, even though the correction would reinforce rather than reverse the conclusion that price exceeds value.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE tax reconciliation, remove the $49 million reorganization benefit and non-recurring purchased-credit benefit if included, separate the recurring German statutory-rate effect from remeasurement benefits, and rerun all scenarios using a sustainable cash tax burden.

audit_findings.title: Transformation costs may have been mislabeled as one-offs
audit_findings.magnitude: $55 million of 2025 acquisition/divestiture-related costs and $178 million of restructuring costs, versus $95 million and $108 million respectively in 2024. If the full $233 million were added back to anchor OE, retaining it as expense would reduce bear/base/bull values by approximately $3.26/$3.85/$4.55 per share and the base buy-below threshold by approximately $2.70 per share.
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back recurring transaction, integration or restructuring expenditures inflates normalized OE and capitalizes the overstatement through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the current year also included $56 million of acquisition and divestiture-related costs compared with $95 million during the year ended December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: Repeated spending is demonstrated by two consecutive years of filed costs, but wholesale addition to OE is not demonstrated without the calculator workpapers. The potential scale is material: $233 million is 12.6% of anchor OE and would change base value by roughly 11.4% if fully added back. The sustainable portion remains unresolved and may be less than the full sensitivity.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every 2025 OE add-back for acquisition, divestiture, integration and restructuring costs; classify expenditures by recurrence and necessity, retain the sustainable portion as an operating expense, and rerun the valuation.
